## Why We Exist
Ever wondered why most brands hide their ingredient list, in microscopic font, at the back? Why you’re made to stare, squint eyed, at the crimp, just to figure out what your food is made of?
As an obese kid trying to eat healthy, I used to ask these questions everyday. I never got an answer, so I did my own research.
Brands hide what goes into their food, because they have something to hide.
Because they’d rather have you drool over fake pictures of molten, drippy chocolate, than have you discover that your food contains artificial sugars and preservatives and other hard-to-pronounce chemicals.
In the name of ‘healthy’, we’re being sold a bunch of lies. And I was done being lied to. So I, along with a few like-minded (and equally betrayed) folks, started The Whole Truth.
Our purpose is simple. We make food so clean, we can proudly declare every single ingredient that goes into it, upfront. And we can speak the whole truth, because we have #nothingtohide.
Shashank Founder. CEO. Obese kid. Fit adult. Hell bent on setting packaged food right.
Who is this guy?
Shashank, our main man, started his fitness journey at over 100kgs, 15 years ago. In the decade that followed, he taught himself fitness, lost 40kgs, ran several marathons, and helped many friends and colleagues get onto the fitness bandwagon.
After all the years of research and self-experimentation, he believes there’s only one universal food truth
good food is made of good ingredients
You can access all his learnings at FITSHIT.in, his free-forever fitness blog read by thousands every week.
Disclaimer – views on the blog are personal. so is the crusade.

faqs.question: Do I need protein powder even if I don't go to the gym?
faqs.answer: Protein powder isn't just for people who workout regularly. While protein is essential for muscle repair and growth, it's also important for overall health, regardless of whether you hit the gym or not. Protein plays a crucial role in various bodily functions, including supporting a healthy immune system, promoting satiety, and aiding in the production of enzymes and hormones. Additionally, protein is crucial for healthy skin, hair, and nails, and maintaining energy levels throughout the day. So, even if you don't work out, your body still needs protein to function properly. If you're already getting enough protein from your regular diet, you may not necessarily need to supplement with protein powder. However, if you find it challenging to meet your daily protein requirements through food alone, protein powder can be a convenient option to help you bridge that gap.

faqs.question: How much protein do I need in a day?
faqs.answer: Start with your body weight. ICMR-NIN (India's National Institute of Nutrition) sets the minimum for a healthy adult at about 0.83 g of protein per kg of body weight a day. So a 70 kg adult needs at least 58 g. If you work out regularly, or want to hold on to muscle while losing fat, aim higher, around 1.2-1.6 g per kg. For the same 70 kg person, that's 84-112 g a day.

faqs.question: What are BCAAs and EAAs?
faqs.answer: Protein is built from 20 amino acids. 9 of them are essential amino acids (EAAs): your body can't make them, so they have to come from food. BCAAs are three of those nine: leucine, isoleucine and valine. They help limit muscle breakdown and support recovery, and leucine matters most, because it's the signal that tells your muscles to start repairing. A protein's quality comes down to how much of each EAA it gives you, which is why we print both numbers on the pack. Whey is naturally rich in both, so you get them from the protein itself, with nothing added.

faqs.question: Can my body use more than 25-30 g of protein in one go?
faqs.answer: Yes. Your body digests and absorbs all the protein you eat, so none of it simply goes to waste. What's true is that around 20-40 g of good-quality protein per meal is enough to fully switch on muscle repair. Eating more in one sitting is still used by your body, just not as efficiently for muscle. So it works better to spread your protein across 3-4 meals through the day.

faqs.question: Will whey protein make me bulky?
faqs.answer: No. Whey protein itself is not a magic formula for muscle growth. Muscle growth happens as a combination of exercise, diet, genetics and time. This protein simply helps you meet your daily protein requirement, and will not lead to anyone bulking up overnight.

faqs.question: Can teenagers have this protein?
faqs.answer: Yes, this protein is safe for teenagers. However, it is formulated primarily for adults, and a teenager's protein needs are different. So we recommend consulting your general physician before adding it to their diet. It is not intended to replace meals and should be used as a supplement to a balanced diet.

faqs.question: Can I give this protein to my parents or older family members?
faqs.answer: Yes, you absolutely can. In fact, protein becomes even more important as we grow older. With age, our bodies naturally lose muscle mass, which can affect strength, balance and overall mobility. Getting enough protein helps slow this muscle loss and supports daily energy levels. That said, it's best to start with a smaller serving and see how their body responds. If they have any existing medical conditions or dietary restrictions, check with their doctor first.

faqs.question: I'm pregnant or breastfeeding. Can I have this protein?
faqs.answer: Every person's situation is different, and so are their requirements. Please consult your doctor or a healthcare professional before adding any new supplement to your diet.

faqs.question: I have diabetes. Can I have this protein?
faqs.answer: This is an unsweetened variant with no added sugar, so it can be a possible option. However, we advise you to consult your doctor for personalised guidance.

faqs.question: Will protein powder make me gain or lose weight?
faqs.answer: Protein supplements themselves do not directly cause weight gain or loss. In fact, protein is an essential macronutrient that can be a valuable part of a balanced diet, and is helpful for weight management, since it keeps you full for longer. It does, however, require calorie management. Adding protein shakes on top of your regular diet, without adjusting other calories or increasing activity, means consuming more than you burn, which will indirectly cause weight gain.

faqs.question: What's the difference between whey isolate and whey concentrate?
faqs.answer: Whey protein is obtained by extracting protein from milk, using filtration (microfiltration, in our case) to separate proteins from fats and carbs (and lactose); whey concentrate retain some of these, while whey isolate undergoes further refining to remove almost all non-protein components, resulting whey isolate in higher protein concentration (>90%) than whey concentrate (80-90%). That's why people with digestive sensitivity and/or lactose intolerance do well on Isolate whey protein.

faqs.question: How do I make my shake? Water or milk, and how much?
faqs.answer: Add 1 level scoop (35 g) or 1 sachet to 200 ml of cold water or milk in a shaker, shake well for about 30 seconds, and drink it up. Water keeps it light and low in calories. Milk makes it creamier and more filling, and adds a little extra protein and calories of its own. Use a shaker, not a spoon, for a smooth shake with no lumps.

faqs.question: Can I consume 2 scoops per day?
faqs.answer: The number of scoops you can have per day depends on your total protein intake for the day, and how you choose to reach there. You could choose to consume protein-rich foods to cover up all your protein needs, in which case you need not supplement with a protein powder. Else, if you find it difficult to hit your protein goals through food, supplementing with a scoop for two is absolutely fine, in fact great!

faqs.question: Can I use protein powder for cooking?
faqs.answer: Yes, but pick the right one. Whey works best in things that are cold, at room temperature or just lukewarm, like smoothies, overnight oats, curd or a shake. High heat denatures whey: the protein unfolds and firms up, a bit like an egg when you cook it. You still get the same amount of protein, so nutritionally it's fine, but the texture turns clumpy and the taste changes. So for cooking or baking, like chillas, pancakes, muffins or parathas, use our unflavoured plant protein instead. It holds up better to heat and blends easily into the dish.

faqs.question: Will this protein cause bloating, gas or acne?
faqs.answer: Most bloating, gas or acne from protein powder comes down to one of two things: additives or lactose. This protein has no added flavours, artificial sweeteners, gums, thickeners, anti-caking or anti-foaming agents, so it should feel light and easy to digest. And since it's whey isolate, it has less than 0.5 g of lactose per scoop, which most people handle well. If you're very sensitive, or would rather skip dairy altogether, try our plant protein range.

faqs.question: I'm lactose intolerant. Can I have this protein?
faqs.answer: Yes. Whey isolate has minimal traces of lactose, i.e. <0.5 g lactose per scoop, which most lactose-intolerant individuals handle well. However, if your intolerance is severe, our plant-based protein range would be a better option.

faqs.question: What is bromelain, and why is it in my protein?
faqs.answer: One of the reasons protein powders cause bloating and heaviness is that your gut isn't primed to receive protein, in such high concentration, in one go. Bromelain is an enzyme found in pineapple stems that helps break down protein. Less than 1% of the mix, and your protein becomes so much easier to digest. Cheers.

faqs.question: What is lecithin, and why is it in my protein?
faqs.answer: Whey, by nature, is hydrophobic, which means it doesn't mix well with water. That's why it needs to be 'instantised', a fancy word for adding a tiny amount of fat (lecithin) that helps it mix better and makes your protein drink smoooooth!

faqs.question: Does this protein have added sugar?
faqs.answer: No. This protein is unsweetened. The small amount of sugar on the label is lactose, the sugar naturally found in milk.

faqs.question: How do you test your protein, and where can I see the reports?
faqs.answer: We test every batch at NABL-accredited labs for everything: protein content, heavy metals, aflatoxin (M1), microbial contamination, pesticide residues and melamine spiking. All these reports are made public, for each batch, here: tinyurl.com/twtproteinlabtestreports

faqs.question: What is the shelf life of this protein?
faqs.answer: The shelf life is 12 months from the date of manufacturing.

faqs.question: How should I store this protein?
faqs.answer: Store away from direct sunlight in a cool, dry place. Tightly seal the pack after use. Once open, contents can also be stored in an airtight container. Consume within 1-2 months of opening the pack.

faqs.question: Where is the protein powder made?
faqs.answer: It's made right here in India. We source our whey from top global suppliers, then blend and pack our protein powders in India at FSSAI and USFDA-registered facilities. Every batch is tested at NABL-accredited labs before it reaches you. Want to know exactly where your pack was made? Match the batch number on your pack with the facility codes on our manufacturing page: thewholetruthfoods.com/pages/manufacturing

faqs.answer: Whey protein is obtained by extracting protein from milk, using filtration (microfiltration, in our case) to separate proteins from fats and carbs (and lactose); whey concentrate retain some of these, while whey isolate undergoes further refining to remove almost all non-protein components, resulting whey isolate in higher protein concentration (>90%) than whey concentrate (80-90%). That's why people with digestive sensitivity and/or lactose intolerance do well on Isolate whey protein.

faqs.question: How do I make my shake? Water or milk, and how much?
faqs.answer: Add 1 level scoop (35 g) to 200 ml of cold water or milk in a shaker, shake well for about 30 seconds, and drink it up. Water keeps it light and low in calories. Milk makes it creamier and more filling, and adds a little extra protein and calories of its own. Use a shaker, not a spoon, for a smooth shake with no lumps.

faqs.question: Can I consume 2 scoops per day?
faqs.answer: The number of scoops you can have per day depends on your total protein intake for the day, and how you choose to reach there. faqs.question: Can I use protein powder for cooking?
faqs.answer: Yes, but pick the right one. Whey works best in things that are cold, at room temperature or just lukewarm, like smoothies, overnight oats, curd or a shake. High heat denatures whey: the protein unfolds and firms up, a bit like an egg when you cook it. You still get the same amount of protein, so nutritionally it's fine, but the texture turns clumpy and the taste changes. So for cooking or baking, like chillas, pancakes, muffins or parathas, use our unflavoured plant protein instead. It holds up better to heat and blends easily into the dish.

faqs.question: Will this protein cause bloating, gas or acne?

If you are, you might still feel bloated, since whey naturally contains some lactose. Try our whey isolate, which has less than 0.5 g of lactose per scoop, or our plant protein range if you'd rather skip dairy altogether.

faqs.question: I'm lactose intolerant. Can I have this protein?

faqs.question: What is bromelain, and why is it in my protein?

faqs.question: What is lecithin, and why is it in my protein?
faqs.answer: Whey, by nature, is hydrophobic, which means it doesn't mix well with water. That's why it needs to be 'instantised', a fancy word for adding a tiny amount of fat (lecithin) that helps it mix better and makes your protein drink smoooooth!

faqs.question: Does this protein have added sugar?

Protein plays a crucial role in various bodily functions, including supporting a healthy immune system, promoting satiety, and aiding in the production of enzymes and hormones. Additionally, protein is crucial for healthy skin, hair, and nails, and maintaining energy levels throughout the day. So, even if you don't work out, your body still needs protein to function properly. faqs.question: Will protein powder make me gain or lose weight?
faqs.answer: Protein supplements themselves do not directly cause weight gain. In fact, protein is an essential macronutrient that can be a valuable part of a balanced diet, and is helpful for weight management, since it keeps you full for longer. It does, however, require calorie management. Adding protein shakes on top of your regular diet, without adjusting other calories or increasing activity, means consuming more than you burn, which will indirectly cause weight gain.

faqs.question: What's the difference between whey isolate and whey concentrate?
faqs.answer: Whey protein is obtained by extracting protein from milk, using filtration (microfiltration, in our case) to separate proteins from fats and carbs (and lactose); whey concentrate retain some of these, while whey isolate undergoes further refining to remove almost all non-protein components, resulting whey isolate in higher protein concentration (>90%) than whey concentrate (80-90%). That's why people with digestive sensitivity and/or lactose intolerance do well on Isolate whey protein.

faqs.question: How do I make my shake? Water or milk, and how much?
faqs.answer: Add 1 level scoop (35 g) to 200 ml of cold water or milk in a shaker, shake well for about 30 seconds, and drink it up. Water keeps it light and low in calories. Milk makes it creamier and more filling, and adds a little extra protein and calories of its own. Use a shaker, not a spoon, for a smooth shake with no lumps.

faqs.question: Can I consume 2 scoops per day?
faqs.answer: The number of scoops you can have per day depends on your total protein intake for the day, and how you choose to reach there. You could choose to consume protein-rich foods to cover up all your protein needs, in which case you need not supplement with a protein powder. Else, if you find it difficult to hit your protein goals through food, supplementing with a scoop for two is absolutely fine, in fact great!

faqs.question: Can I use protein powder for cooking?
faqs.answer: Yes, but pick the right one. Whey works best in things that are cold, at room temperature or just lukewarm, like smoothies, overnight oats, curd or a shake. High heat denatures whey: the protein unfolds and firms up, a bit like an egg when you cook it. You still get the same amount of protein, so nutritionally it's fine, but the texture turns clumpy and the taste changes. So for cooking or baking, like chillas, pancakes, muffins or parathas, use our unflavoured plant protein instead. It holds up better to heat and blends easily into the dish.

faqs.question: Will this protein cause bloating, gas or acne?
faqs.answer: Most bloating, gas or acne from protein powder comes down to one of two things: additives or lactose. This protein has no added flavours, artificial sweeteners, gums, thickeners, anti-caking or anti-foaming agents, so if you're not lactose intolerant, it should feel light and easy to digest. If you are, you might still feel bloated, since whey naturally contains some lactose. Try our whey isolate, which has less than 0.5 g of lactose per scoop, or our plant protein range if you'd rather skip dairy altogether.

faqs.question: I'm lactose intolerant. Can I have this protein?
faqs.answer: No. If you are lactose intolerant, we would not recommend Unflavoured Whey Concentrate, since it contains whey concentrate, which has lactose. In whey protein, we would recommend our Unflavoured Whey Isolate, since whey isolate has minimal traces of lactose, i.e. <0.5 g lactose per scoop. However, if your intolerance is severe, our plant-based protein range would be a better option.

faqs.question: What is bromelain, and why is it in my protein?
faqs.answer: One of the reasons protein powders cause bloating and heaviness is that your gut isn't primed to receive protein, in such high concentration, in one go. Bromelain is an enzyme found in pineapple stems that helps break down protein. Less than 1% of the mix, and your protein becomes so much easier to digest. Cheers.

faqs.question: What is lecithin, and why is it in my protein?
faqs.answer: Whey, by nature, is hydrophobic, which means it doesn't mix well with water. That's why it needs to be 'instantised', a fancy word for adding a tiny amount of fat (lecithin) that helps it mix better and makes your protein drink smoooooth!

faqs.question: Does this protein have added sugar?
faqs.answer: No. This protein is unsweetened. The small amount of sugar on the label is lactose, the sugar naturally found in milk.

faqs.question: How do you test your protein, and where can I see the reports?
faqs.answer: We test every batch at NABL-accredited labs for everything: protein content, heavy metals, aflatoxin (M1), microbial contamination, pesticide residues and melamine spiking. All these reports are made public, for each batch, here: tinyurl.com/twtproteinlabtestreports

faqs.question: What is the shelf life of this protein?
faqs.answer: The shelf life is 12 months from the date of manufacturing.

faqs.question: How should I store this protein?
faqs.answer: Store away from direct sunlight in a cool, dry place. Tightly seal the pack after use. Once open, contents can also be stored in an airtight container. Consume within 1-2 months of opening the pack.

faqs.question: Where is the protein powder made?
faqs.answer: It's made right here in India. We source our whey from top global suppliers, then blend and pack our protein powders in India at FSSAI and USFDA-registered facilities. Every batch is tested at NABL-accredited labs before it reaches you. Want to know exactly where your pack was made? Match the batch number on your pack with the facility codes on our manufacturing page: thewholetruthfoods.com/pages/manufacturing

Question: Is there added sugar in my muesli?
Answer: Yes. To sweeten these Mueslis we add Kakvi, which is the most unrefined form of sugar possible (and is even more nutritious than jaggery). But it does have a Glycemic Index similar to jaggery. So if you’re completely off sugar or diabetic, please consult your doctor before consuming. PS: We also have a 'No added sugar' muesli now if you'd like.
Question: Is this muesli really ‘high-protein’?
Answer: If you have 3-4 meals a day, ideally, each meal should contribute 25-30% of your protein requirement. Our high protein muesli’s, when had with a bowl of milk (~200ml), do exactly that.
Question: Is this muesli vegan?
Answer: The regular (non-whey) Mueslis are 100% vegan. There is no animal-source ingredient. Even the sweetener is Kakvi (liquid jaggery). Not honey.
Question: Is this muesli gluten free?
Answer: Yes. There’s no wheat or gluten used in the production of these Mueslis.
Question: What’s the best way to consume this Muesli?
Answer: In 200ml cold milk. Or with 150gm curd (or Greek yogurt). Add some fresh fruits like apple, banana, berries or pomegranate on top for extra freshness. Of course, you can just have it as a snack too! But be careful of over-doing it.
Question: What’s the right portion size?
Answer: We recommend 50gms. Enough to satiate you and get you started in the morning. But not so much that it gets you drowsy or busts your calorie quota.
Question: What is Kakvi? Isn’t it just sugar?
Answer: Kakvi is the most un-refined form of sugar possible. It’s the golden dark liquid that, on further reduction, hardens into jaggery. Since we pull it out mid-way, it retains even more nutrition than jaggery. Of course, ~70% of Kakvi is sucrose (sugar). Which means that in terms of insulin impact and glycemic index, it’s similar to sugar. But it’s far more nutritious.
